forces: Two choirs, two orchestras, soloists. Each orchestra: 2 flutes, 2 oboes (also oboe d'amore and oboe da caccia), strings, viola da gamba, continuo
lesson_for_this_work: The model. The new work sets its text again for one voice and one orchestra
The first Passion of Bach that we have complete: the opening chorus has a pedal note of 12 bars (measured)

forces: Choir, soloists, 2 flutes, 2 oboes d'amore, strings, 2 violas da gamba, 2 lutes, continuo
lesson_for_this_work: The sound of the same year as the Passion: flutes, oboes d'amore, gambas, and lutes together

forces: Alto alone; oboe d'amore, 2 violins, viola, obbligato organ, continuo
lesson_for_this_work: A complete work of Bach for one alto: five movements, arias and recitatives in turn, a pastoral first aria on repeated eighth notes
The first church cantata of Bach for one voice. It starts with a dissonant chord. Low range and tessitura for the alto

forces: Bass alone (a version for soprano with a flute, about 1731); oboe, strings, continuo
lesson_for_this_work: A solo cantata of the year of the Passion: one voice with one obbligato instrument
Bach made a new work from a work of a different composer: Pergolesi's Stabat Mater with a German psalm text and more orchestral material

work: Canonic Variations on "Vom Himmel hoch", BWV 769
lesson_for_this_work: Five variations in canon on one chorale tune: the model for chorale and canon together
Canons and fugues on one given theme. One canon goes up one whole tone at each repeat

work: Mass in B minor, BWV 232: Crucifixus
lesson_for_this_work: A chorus on a ground bass that goes down by semitones: the bass has 70 percent repeated notes and 21 percent semitone moves (measured)
The old form before Bach: the Gospel story with no instruments and no arias

forces: Alto alone; violins 1 and 2, violas, continuo
lesson_for_this_work: Passion music for one alto and strings. F minor; slow in all movements but the Amen; movements 4 to 6 have the music of movements 1 to 3

forces: Alto alone; strings, organ or harpsichord
lesson_for_this_work: A long work for one alto. A contralto or a countertenor can sing the part

forces: Soprano, alto; violins 1 and 2, viola, continuo
lesson_for_this_work: Passion music for solo voices and a small string group

work: Performance of the St Matthew Passion in Berlin
lesson_for_this_work: The first well-known new version: Mendelssohn changed parts of the work for the taste of his time. A new version for a new time has a long history
A late, bare Passion work with few forces
Music of the 18th century with new rhythm, new harmony, and new colours: the old notes stay in view

work: Fuga (Ricercata) a 6 voci, from The Musical Offering
lesson_for_this_work: Each voice of the fugue goes from instrument to instrument in short pieces: the colours show the motifs
A chorale of Bach in a twelve-note work. The last section is a set of chorale variations. The row has triads: its first three notes are a G minor triad
Bach's canons with new lines added: old counterpoint and new counterpoint in one texture
Almost fully atonal; a major triad comes only two times. The last chord is E major. A plain triad is a strong event after dissonance
Collage: old tonal music against twelve-note music
A baroque form with more than one style at the same time (polystylism)
A canon in A minor on one motif. It starts and ends with written silence
Variations on a theme of six bars: "frantic activity and sublime stillness"
A theme of Bach loses one note at each end in each variation. At the end the theme comes back note by note, backwards

forces: Bass (Jesus), tenor (Pilate), vocal quartet (Evangelist), choir, violin, oboe, cello, bassoon, organ
lesson_for_this_work: The text makes the rhythm. Each person has a note value and a pitch centre. One voice goes by step, one voice has the notes of a triad
The form of the Passions of Bach with a different story (the life of Bach)
One chorale phrase of Bach; then each voice sings the same phrase in a different tempo. All voices wait at the end of the phrase
Canons on one short text, with the sound of medieval polyphony

forces: Soloists, choir, orchestra with Latin and African percussion
lesson_for_this_work: One of four new Passions for the Bach year 2000 (with Rihm, Gubaidulina, and Tan Dun). A Passion can speak in the musical language of its composer
The Gospel text together with a second text (the Book of Revelation)

forces: Soloists, choir, strings, percussion with water
lesson_for_this_work: A Passion after Matthew for the same project: ritual sounds in place of the baroque orchestra

forces: 4 voices (soprano, alto, tenor, bass); each singer plays simple percussion
lesson_for_this_work: The format of the St Matthew Passion with 15 numbers in 35 minutes: story numbers and response numbers in turn. "There is no Bach in my piece"
The Passion chorale of the St Matthew Passion comes into view at about the middle. "Saturating the palette with classicism while denying it form"
Richter removed 75 percent of the material of Vivaldi. The parts that stay are in loops and in phase shifts
The movement types of the baroque suite with the vocal sounds of today
Three new songs for one mezzo-soprano and an orchestra of period instruments. The orchestra asks for new music for old instruments since 2016
A large new work for voices and an orchestra of period instruments
